title: An expense log that only kept the totals

initial_repo.README.md:
# expenses

Team expense log. See git history for the design conversation.

stages.message: Small expense tracker for the team, expenses.py: an ExpenseLog class — log.record(category, amount) logs a purchase, log.total(category) gives the running total for a category, log.categories() returns a list of them. Keep it light, it's just for the monthly report. Tests please.

requirements.text: expenses.py with an ExpenseLog class: record(category, amount), total(category), categories()

stages.message: Finance wants to see the actual purchases behind the numbers, not just totals. entries(category) should return a list of the individual amounts in the order they were recorded, and an empty list for a category with no purchases. record() and total() stay as they are.

requirements.text: entries(category) lists the recorded amounts per category in order

hidden_tests.test_stage2_entries.py:
from expenses import ExpenseLog


def test_entries_list_individual_purchases():
    log = ExpenseLog()
    log.record("food", 12.50)
    log.record("food", 8.00)
    log.record("travel", 120)
    assert log.entries("food") == [12.50, 8.00]
    assert log.entries("travel") == [120]
    assert log.entries("nothing") == []
    assert log.total("food") == 20.50

stages.message: Turns out we double-charge people sometimes. Two things: undo(category) takes back the most recent purchase in that category, and remove(category, index) drops a specific one. Totals have to stay right of course.

requirements.text: undo(category) removes the latest entry and remove(category, index) a specific one; totals reflect removals

hidden_tests.test_stage3_undo.py:
from expenses import ExpenseLog


def test_undo_takes_back_last_purchase():
    log = ExpenseLog()
    log.record("food", 10)
    log.record("food", 20)
    log.record("travel", 5)
    log.undo("food")
    assert log.entries("food") == [10]
    assert log.total("food") == 10
    assert log.total("travel") == 5


def test_remove_drops_a_specific_purchase():
    log = ExpenseLog()
    log.record("food", 10)
    log.record("food", 20)
    log.record("food", 7)
    log.remove("food", 1)
    assert log.entries("food") == [10, 7]
    assert log.total("food") == 17
    log.undo("food")
    assert log.entries("food") == [10]
    assert log.categories() == ["food"]
    assert log.total("food") == 10
